headline: DAHD Strengthens Surveillance, Vaccination and Disease-Control Measures to Contain Lumpy Skin Disease
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

DAHD Strengthens Surveillance, Vaccination and Disease-Control Measures to Contain Lumpy Skin Disease

08 SEP 2026 10:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, has taken proactive measures to strengthen the prevention, surveillance and control of Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) in the country. The Department is closely coordinating with States/UTs to assess the disease situation and ensure timely implementation of vaccination and other disease-control measures.

During the recent review, States/UTs were advised to ensure timely vaccination, particularly of heifers and young cattle, along with ring vaccination, movement control, isolation of affected animals, vector control, disinfection and sanitary measures, management of stray animals, treatment of affected animals and quarantine of newly introduced animals. States were also advised to ensure timely and transparent reporting of disease incidents through official channels.

A Central Expert Team was deputed to Uttar Pradesh in August 2026 to assess the disease situation on the ground, monitor the measures being undertaken by the State and provide technical guidance for preparedness and response. The Department has also been maintaining close monitoring of the disease situation across States/UTs. Review meetings with States/UTs were held on 27th August 2026 and 7th September 2026 to review the situation and strengthen preparedness and response measures.

Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) is a viral disease affecting cattle and buffaloes, caused by the Capripox virus and transmitted mainly through arthropod vectors. The disease is characterised by fever and skin nodules and is generally associated with low mortality. In India, LSD was first reported in West Bengal and Odisha in September 2019.

Since July 2026, sporadic cases of LSD have been reported mainly from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, Uttarakhand and a few other States, particularly among young animals and calves. The disease has shown very low severity, and affected animals are generally recovering within a week.

The Department has been providing technical advisories and guidelines to States/UTs on vaccination, treatment, biosecurity and disease-control measures. Diagnostic and testing capacity for LSD has also been strengthened across the country with technical support from ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal, and a network of laboratories, including Regional Disease Diagnostic Laboratories (RDDLs) and the Central Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (CDDL).

To further strengthen national capacity for the prevention and control of LSD, the Department has provided financial assistance to States/UTs for vaccination, training and awareness generation, besides strengthening veterinary laboratory infrastructure and capacity building of the veterinary workforce.

More than 36.18 crore cattle have been vaccinated/re-vaccinated against LSD so far. Vaccination and other disease-control measures are continuing across affected States/UTs, along with preventive measures in non-affected States/UTs.

The LSD situation in the country is presently under control, with a substantial decline in the severity of infection and mortality. At present, there are 3,461 active cases, mainly among young and unvaccinated animals and animals with co-morbidities.

The Department continues to closely monitor the situation and provide necessary technical guidance, vaccination support, diagnostic and laboratory support, and financial assistance to States/UTs for effective control and containment of the disease.

headline: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan visits Nyedar Namlo in Itanagar; highlights need to preserve indigenous faith, culture and knowledge systems
fullText:
Vice President's Secretariat

Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan visits Nyedar Namlo in Itanagar; highlights need to preserve indigenous faith, culture and knowledge systems

Tribal communities are not merely custodians of India’s past, but partners in building its future: Vice-President

‘Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi’: Vice President underscores PM Narendra Modi’s vision for indigenous communities

Arunachal Pradesh embodies India’s unity in diversity, where traditions and modern aspirations walk together: Vice-President

09 SEP 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today visited Nyedar Namlo in Itanagar, a sacred place of worship and community hub associated with the indigenous Donyi-Polo faith of the Nyishi community and other indigenous groups of Arunachal Pradesh.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visited Nyedar Namlo in Itanagar today, a sacred place of worship and community hub associated with the indigenous Donyi-Polo faith of the Nyishi community and other indigenous groups of Arunachal Pradesh.

The Vice-President offered… pic.twitter.com/iRHxfwgqoD

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 9, 2026

The Vice-President offered prayers at the prayer hall and was briefed on the Nyishi indigenous faith, beliefs and prayer systems, the Yerko indigenous Gurukul system, preservation of traditional knowledge and medicinal practices, and efforts to promote the mother tongue.

Addressing a community gathering, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said he felt blessed to visit Nyedar Namlo during his first visit to Arunachal Pradesh. He said he was honoured to be at a place “where traditions become modern thinking, and modern thinking is not destroying traditions.”

He described Arunachal Pradesh as a proud embodiment of India’s unity in diversity, where ancient traditions and modern aspirations walk together. He also said that the people of Arunachal Pradesh stand as proud sentinels of India’s territorial integrity.

Highlighting the values of the Donyi-Polo tradition, the Vice-President said its emphasis on nature, truth, harmony and community remains deeply relevant to the modern world. He stressed that development must go hand in hand with cultural preservation.

Appreciating the efforts of the Nyishi Nyidung Mung-jwng Rallung, he said its work in documentation, research, traditional festivals, cultural activities and preservation of customary laws and social values is making an important contribution to the community’s cultural future.

He also highlighted the Yerko Gurukul system, saying it offers an important model of combining contemporary education with indigenous knowledge, enabling children to embrace modern opportunities while remaining connected to their roots.

Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi”, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said tribal communities are not merely custodians of India’s past but important partners in building its future. He noted that the recognition of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas has brought renewed national attention to the invaluable contributions of India’s tribal communities. He also linked preservation of indigenous traditions with the spirit of Vocal for Local and Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat.

“Preservation of indigenous culture is not about resisting change. It is about ensuring that change does not come at the cost of identity,” he said.

Calling upon the youth to embrace modern science, technology and global skills while remaining connected to their mother tongue and traditions, the Vice-President said India must be modern in its aspirations but deeply rooted in its civilisational and cultural values.

He extended his best wishes to the Nyedar Namlo movement and expressed hope that the sacred place would continue to inspire peace, harmony, respect for nature, social unity and a strong sense of community.

Among those present on the occasion were Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik, Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Member of Parliament Shri Tai Tagak, Minister for Home and Indigenous Affairs Shri Mama Natung and Chief Secretary Shri Manish Kumar Gupta.

headline: India endorses the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security; Department of Telecommunications to take the initiative forward
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

India endorses the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security; Department of Telecommunications to take the initiative forward

Announcement made on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial at Chapel Hill, North Carolina

India joins over 20 like-minded governments in a shared commitment to open, interoperable, secure and resilient next-generation networks

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India aims to contribute 10 percent of 6G Global Standards and Patents

Initiative to advance Union Minister of Communications and DoNER Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia’s commitment to position India as a global leader in 6G

09 SEP 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi

India has endorsed the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, joining a group of like-minded governments that have committed to shaping the sixth generation of wireless communications on the principles of openness, interoperability, security, resilience, resource efficiency and innovation-led competition.

The initiative will advance the vision of Union Minister of Communications and DoNER Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, who has always emphasised that India is committed to leading the world in 6G. This also highlights the significance laid by Minister of State for Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani on the country’s transformation from a technology adopter to a standard-setter.

Emphasising the significance of the announcement, the Union Minister for Communications took to social media to share his views on the development.

Bharat For 6G! 🇮🇳

An absolute delight to announce India’s endorsement of the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security , joining 24 like-minded nations in advancing an open, interoperable, secure and resilient next-generation network.

This global partnership will help…

— Jyotiraditya M. Scindia (@JM_Scindia) September 9, 2026

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) will take forward India’s engagement under the Call to Action and coordinate the relevant follow-up activities with concerned government agencies, industry, academia and other stakeholders. India joins other governments that have affirmed the Call to Action, including Canada, Costa Rica, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, France, Germany, Greece, Honduras, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Norway, Paraguay, the Republic of Korea, Romania, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The endorsement was announced on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial, held in North Carolina, United States, on 1-2 September 2026 under the United States’ G20 Presidency. The announcement was marked by a handshake between Shri Jitin Prasada, Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry, and Electronics and Information Technology in the Government of India, and Mr. Howard Lutnick, United States Secretary of Commerce.

Under the Call to Action, participating governments affirm that secure digital infrastructure is essential to technological competitiveness, economic prosperity and national security, and that advanced telecommunications networks are both the gateway to and the heart of that infrastructure. The initiative recognises that next-generation networks will underpin major economic and societal activity and the delivery of critical services; that globally interconnected communications systems can introduce cyber, economic and national security risks, making strong baselines for network security and resilience a shared responsibility; and that shaping the future of 6G calls for concerted action in collaboration with industry, academia and other stakeholders.

The Call to Action sets out a graduated set of steps for participating governments. Within one month, each government is to identify and designate expert 6G points of contact, designate the agency responsible for managing communications with the contact group, and prepare a preliminary list of relevant industry and academic stakeholders. Within three months, governments are to engage the telecommunications sector to map the emerging landscape for secure and interoperable 6G, identify barriers to leadership, convene to examine their findings, and begin identifying the economic, political and financial resources that could support 6G competitiveness. Within six months, they are to strategise at expert level on supporting secure, resilient, sustainable and innovative 6G supply chains over the long term, and to consider how 6G leadership and security may be reflected in national and regional strategies. Within twelve months, participants are to convene in person in 2027 to review progress, exchange lessons learned and best practices, and set priorities for the following year alongside relevant industry stakeholders.

Further avenues identified for cooperation include coordination and information-sharing on 6G research and development; collaboration among trade and development finance agencies to support the deployment of secure and resilient 5G and 6G technologies in global markets; assessment of technical and strategic cybersecurity risks associated with telecommunications sector investments; greater transparency on supply chain developments and vulnerabilities; realising the full potential of 5G systems for industrial, commercial, security and defense applications; and working with industry to shape global 6G standards, including strong security standards, in standards development organisations.

The Call to Action expressly provides that participation does not bind or limit any government’s authority to pursue its own independent positioning or autonomy in relation to industry-driven standards bodies, and that each participant’s next steps will vary according to its own national priorities, resources and capabilities. It also cautions against duplicating the technical work already under way in industry-led standardisation fora.

India joins other governments that have affirmed the Call to Action, including Canada, Costa Rica, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, France, Germany, Greece, Honduras, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Norway, Paraguay, the Republic of Korea, Romania, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) will take forward India’s engagement under the Call to Action and coordinate the relevant follow-up activities with concerned government agencies, industry, academia and other stakeholders.

India’s participation builds on an established domestic foundation, including the Bharat 6G Vision, the Bharat 6G Alliance and the indigenous 4G and 5G technology stack. In line with the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of Viksit Bharat 2047, engagement under the Call to Action will complement India’s ongoing work in international standardisation and spectrum fora, and is without prejudice to India’s independent positions in those fora.

headline: Cabinet approves five multitracking projects covering 17 Districts across the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 540 Kms
fullText:
Ministry of Railways

Cabinet approves five multitracking projects covering 17 Districts across the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 540 Kms

The total estimated cost of the projects is Rs. 10,021 crore and planned to be completed up to 2029-30

09 SEP 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved five projects of Ministry of Railways with total cost of Rs. 10,021 crore (approx.). These projects include:

Arakkonam – Renigunta 3rd and 4th Line – 77 kms

Whitefield – Bangarapet 3rd and 4th Line – 47 kms

Hosur – Omalur Doubling – 147 kms

Salem – Karur – Dindigul Doubling – 159 kms

Multitracking of Secunderabad (Ghatkesar) – Kazipet – 110 kms

The increased line capacity will significantly enhance mobility, resulting in improved operational efficiency and service reliability for Indian Railways. These multi-tracking projects are poised to streamline operations and alleviate congestion. The projects are in line with the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Vision of a New India which will make people of the region “Atmanirbhar” by way of comprehensive development in the area which will enhance their employment/ self-employment opportunities.

The projects are planned on PM-Gati Shakti National Master Plan with focus on enhancing multi-modal connectivity and logistic efficiency through integrated planning and stakeholder consultations. These projects will provide seamless connectivity for movement of people, goods, and services.

The five projects covering 17 Districts across the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, will increase the existing network of Indian Railways by about 540 Kms. The approved multi-tracking projects will enhance connectivity to approx. 2,121 villages, which are having a population of about 52 lakhs.

The approved capacity enhancement will improve rail connectivity to several prominent tourist destinations across the country, including Tirupati, Subramaniya Swamy Temple (Tiruttani), Sri Padmavati Ammavaari Temple (Tiruchanur), Kotilingeshwara Devaalaya, Sri Seethi Byraveshwara Swamy Temple, Bangaru Tirupati, Kolar Gold Fields, Hogennakkal Falls, Hosur Fort, Mettur Dam, Kodaikanal Hills, Sathyamangalam Wildlife Sanctuary, Namakkal Anjaneyar Temple, Namakkal Fort, Kalyana Pasupatheswar Temple, Yadagirigutta Temple, Bhongir Fort, Surendrapuri, Swarnagiri Temple, etc.

These projects are essential routes for transportation of commodities such as coal, cement, iron and steel, container, automobile, food grains, petroleum products, fertilizers, etc. The capacity augmentation works will result in additional freight traffic of magnitude 47 MTPA (Million Tonnes Per Annum). The Railways being environment friendly and energy efficient mode of transportation, will help both in achieving climate goals and minimizing logistics cost of the country, reduce oil import (~8 crore Litres) and lower CO2 emissions (~42 crore Kg) which is equivalent to plantation of ~2 crore trees.

(Release ID: 2308264)

Cabinet approves three multitracking projects covering 14 Districts across the states of West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 656 Kms

The total estimated cost of the projects is Rs. 10,783 crore and planned to be completed up to 2029-30

09 SEP 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved 03 (Three) projects of Ministry of Railways with total cost of Rs. 10,783 crore. These projects include:

Kharagpur – Jharsuguda (Bagdehi) 4th Line

Katni – Pendra Road 4th Line

Bilaspur (Uslapur) – Pendra Road 3rd Line

headline: International Deep-sea Macrofauna Taxonomy School Commences at CMLRE, Kochi under ISA and MoES Collaboration
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

International Deep-sea Macrofauna Taxonomy School Commences at CMLRE, Kochi under ISA and MoES Collaboration

09 SEP 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi

Kochi, 07 September 2026 — The Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE), operating under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Government of India, has officially commenced the five-day “Deep-sea Macrofauna Taxonomy School: Standardizing Methodologies for Biodiversity Assessments” in Kochi. Running from September 07–11, 2026, the prestigious capacity-building initiative is organized under the Sustainable Seabed Knowledge Initiative (SSKI) platform of the International Seabed Authority (ISA).

The program is a collaborative effort involving CMLRE (MoES), the International Seabed Authority (ISA), the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), and the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea (MABIK).

Inaugural Highlights and Leadership Addresses

The inaugural ceremony was graced by Her Excellency Ms. Leticia Carvalho, Secretary-General of the International Seabed Authority (ISA), as the Chief Guest. Delivering an inspirational address, Ms. Carvalho emphasized the critical need to strengthen scientific knowledge and taxonomic expertise to underpin sound environmental management of the deep seabed. She underscored the role of international cooperation and standardized scientific approaches among member states, while encouraging early-career researchers to cultivate scientific excellence, perseverance, and confidence when embracing complex challenges.

Earlier, the welcome address was delivered by Dr. R. Maheskumar, Head of CMLRE. The inaugural session featured a comprehensive presentation on the multi-spectrum marine biodiversity research activities of CMLRE by Dr. Senthil, Scientist-E, CMLRE, followed by a Special Lecture on marine biodiversity studies under MoES's Deep Ocean Mission by Dr. G. Dharani, Scientist-G & Head of the Marine Biotechnology Division at NIOT, Chennai. The ceremony also spotlighted institutional activities and commitments under the SSKI program by MABIK, Republic of Korea, alongside a keynote address by Dr. Baban Ingole, former Scientist at NIO, Goa, focusing on benthic studies in the Indian Ocean.

Global Participation and Technical Scope

The training program brings together approximately 30 early-career researchers and scientists from ISA Member States within the Indian Ocean Region (IORA). Participating nations include South Africa, Kenya, Bangladesh, Mauritius, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Mozambique, Tanzania, Thailand, Oman, and India.

Over the five-day intensive curriculum, participants will engage in:

Specialized lectures, field visits, and benthic sample collection

Hands-on laboratory training in macrofauna identification and result reporting

Advanced technical instruction in traditional taxonomy, DNA barcoding, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and biodiversity data analysis

Workshops on sample curation and open-access biodiversity data publishing

Guidance is being provided by eminent national and international resource persons hailing from Brazil, South Korea, Portugal, Sweden, Mauritius, Indonesia, Germany, and Singapore, alongside experts from collaborating Indian institutions and CMLRE.

Strategic Importance

Hosting this landmark ISA capacity-building program reinforces India’s growing leadership in deep-sea biodiversity research. By standardizing methodologies for benthic biodiversity assessment and fostering robust international scientific partnerships, the initiative marks a significant step forward in sustainable Indian Ocean exploration and environmental governance.

headline: Raksha Mantri pays a courtesy call on Sri Lankan President in Colombo
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

Raksha Mantri pays a courtesy call on Sri Lankan President in Colombo

India and Sri Lanka reaffirm commitment to shared progress & people welfare while ensuring regional security and prosperity

As closest friend and neighbour, India considers it a responsibility to provide assistance as first responder, will continue to do so: Shri Rajnath Singh

Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to India’s security interests: Mr Anura Kumara Dissanayake

Both sides ink MoUs on upgradation of L70 Guns for Sri Lankan Air Force and cooperation between National Cadet Corps & National Defence Colleges of the two countries

Three Bailey Bridges constructed by the Indian Defence Forces virtually inaugurated

09 SEP 2026 2:39PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh called on the President of Sri Lanka Mr Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo on September 09, 2026. The two leaders held substantive discussions on issues covering the entire spectrum of the multi-faceted partnership between the two nations, characterised by traditionally warm relations and mutual trust.

The two sides reaffirmed that as civilisational twins, close neighbours & maritime partners, India and Sri Lanka would continue to work together for their development & welfare of the people while working jointly to ensure the safety, security, peace and prosperity of the region. Raksha Mantri conveyed greetings on behalf of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and underlined that the citizens of the two countries share deep friendship based on strong historical & civilisational links and people-to-people exchanges.

Extending a warm welcome to Raksha Mantri, President Dissanayake recalled his interactions with PM Modi and reiterated that Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for any activities inimical to India’s security interests.

President Dissanayake expressed his gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Operation Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New Delhi to facilitate reconstruction and rehabilitation work across different parts of the island. Raksha Mantri emphasised that as a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, India considered it not a favour, but a responsibility to provide assistance as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future as well.

Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey Bridges constructed by the Indian Defence Forces. The two sides also exchanged MoUs on upgradation of L70 Guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force, and cooperation between National Cadet Corps (NCC) & National Defence Colleges (NDC) of both the countries. The MoU on Upgradation of six L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force falls under a Government of India grant. The upgradation of these air defence guns will significantly strengthen the air defence architecture of critical assets in Sri Lanka. These air defence guns were earlier provided to the Sri Lanka Air Force by India.

The MoU on academic cooperation between NDC, India and NDC, Sri Lanka will facilitate knowledge sharing which will be a significant step in further strengthening the academic bonds between both the sister institutes. The MoU on NCC cooperation will formalise the NCC youth exchange programme between India and Sri Lanka. This exchange programme provides a valuable opportunity for NCC cadets from multiple countries across the world to come to New Delhi every year and participate in NCC events.

headline: MC²+ to Launch Dedicated Co-working Space and Innovation Node at NRL Centre, Guwahati Tomorrow
fullText:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

MC²+ to Launch Dedicated Co-working Space and Innovation Node at NRL Centre, Guwahati Tomorrow

New facility to offer 50+ workstations, 16 cabins, investor and technical consultant rooms to boost startup ecosystem in the Northeast

09 SEP 2026 2:02PM by PIB Delhi

MC²+ will tomorrow launch a dedicated Node and Co-working Space on the 6th Floor of the NRL Centre, Guwahati, marking a significant step in its efforts to strengthen India's startup and innovation ecosystem, with particular focus on the Northeast.

Located in the heart of Guwahati, the new facility has been envisioned as a vibrant, collaborative and professionally equipped environment for startups, entrepreneurs and innovators. Designed around the evolving needs of emerging ventures, it brings together best-in-class infrastructure, professional support, technical expertise, investor access and industry connections under one roof.

The facility offers 50+ dedicated workstations, 16 cabins, 4 investor meeting rooms and 2 technical consultant rooms, along with 2 meeting rooms, a full-fledged cafeteria and common areas. The infrastructure has been designed and developed as a best-in-class facility, benchmarked against leading startup and innovation spaces nationally, giving startups a professional and contemporary environment to work, collaborate and grow.

The investor rooms will provide dedicated spaces for founders to present their ideas, engage with potential investors and explore opportunities for funding and strategic partnerships. The technical consultant rooms will facilitate focused interactions with experts, enabling startups to seek guidance on technology development, product refinement and technical challenges.

The value of the space extends well beyond its physical infrastructure. MC²+ will provide startups with access to a comprehensive support ecosystem comprising domain experts, technical consultants, legal advisors, and specialised finance and audit consultants — enabling entrepreneurs to seek professional guidance across critical areas such as technology and product development, intellectual property, contracts and regulatory requirements, financial planning, accounting, audit preparedness, compliance and business structuring.

Beyond the formal workspaces, a full-fledged cafeteria and café pantry have been designed to encourage informal interactions and networking, providing an environment where entrepreneurs can take a break, exchange ideas and build connections that can evolve into meaningful collaborations.

The vision behind the initiative is to create an environment where startups can access much more than a place to work — a platform where they can find the infrastructure, expertise, mentorship, professional guidance and connections required at different stages of their journey.

The establishment of the MC²+ Node at NRL Centre, Guwahati, marks an important step towards strengthening the startup and innovation ecosystem in Guwahati and the Northeast. It aims to bring together entrepreneurs, experts, investors and industry stakeholders, creating an environment where ideas can move from conception to development, validation and scale.

The formal inauguration will take place tomorrow, September 10, 2026, at the NRL Centre, Guwahati.

headline: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses Special Session of Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly
fullText:
Vice President's Secretariat

Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses Special Session of Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly

‘Rashtra Pratham’ and ‘Viksit Bharat @ 2047’ Must Guide Legislative Work: Vice-President

‘Debates, Discussions or Even Disruptions Must Lead to a Decision’: Vice President

Arunachal Pradesh’s Progress Is Integral to India’s Development and Security: Vice-President

Responsible Utilisation of Arunachal Pradesh’s Hydropower Potential Can Boost State Revenue and Development: Vice-President

09 SEP 2026 1:46PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Special Session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly in Itanagar, calling upon legislators to uphold the highest traditions of democracy and work towards the development of the State and the nation.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Special Session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly in Itanagar today, and called upon the legislators to uphold the highest traditions of democracy and work towards the development of the State and the nation.

The… pic.twitter.com/DqaslGe58V

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 9, 2026

On his arrival at the Assembly premises, the Vice-President paid floral tributes to the statues of Mahatma Gandhi and Babasaheb Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and was accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour. He also visited the Arunachal Pradesh Assembly Museum, which showcases the evolution and growth of the State Legislature and its legislative journey.

Addressing the Assembly, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that Arunachal Pradesh has immense strategic importance, rich cultural heritage and abundant natural resources, and plays a vital role in safeguarding the nation’s borders. He noted that the security of the rest of the country is closely linked to the protection of the borders by the people of Arunachal Pradesh.

Emphasising India’s unity amid its diversity, the Vice-President said that the country is united by one Constitution, one vision of ‘Rashtra Pratham’ (Nation First) and one goal of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Quoting national poet Subramania Bharati, he highlighted the unity of thought underlying India’s diverse languages and traditions.

Recalling India’s rich democratic heritage, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan described India as the ‘Mother of Democracy’ and urged legislators to live up to this legacy.

The Vice-President highlighted the growing focus on the development of the North-East, recalling the establishment of the Ministry of DoNER during the tenure of former Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee and the emphasis on the region under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Act East Policy. He congratulated the Government and people of Arunachal Pradesh for the State’s development achievements, including its emergence as the country’s leading producer of kiwi, expansion of road infrastructure, issuance of over one lakh Soil Health Cards and significant progress in education and per capita income.

Congratulating the State Legislature on completing its Golden Jubilee, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated initiatives such as making the Legislative Secretariat plastic-free and establishing the Assembly Library and Museum.

Urging legislators to place public service above electoral success, the Vice-President said that elections may be won through votes, but the respect and trust of people can only be earned through dedicated service. He called upon Members to make effective use of Question Hour and Zero Hour to raise issues concerning public policy and their constituencies.

As the Presiding Officer of the Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised the importance of dialogue, debate and discussion in legislative functioning. Reiterating his message that “debates, discussions, or even disruptions must always lead to a decision,” he said that healthy debate strengthens democracy and constructive cooperation advances the State and the nation.

The Vice-President said that there can be no Viksit Bharat without a Viksit Arunachal Pradesh, stressing that development must be inclusive and no tribal or marginalised community should be left behind. He also emphasised the need to balance environmental concerns with responsible utilisation of natural resources for the economic development and welfare of the people. Referring to Arunachal Pradesh’s significant hydropower potential, he said its appropriate utilisation could generate greater revenue and accelerate the State’s development.

Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik, Speaker of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly Shri Tesam Pongte, Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Members of the Legislative Assembly, senior officials of the State Government and Legislative Secretariat were present on the occasion.

Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches India’s Advanced Ocean Research Vessel ‘ORV Sagar Manthan’ to Drive Indigenous Maritime Research

09 SEP 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi

Kolkata, September 09, 2026 — Marking a historic milestone in India’s journey toward self-reliance in oceanographic science and maritime technology, the state-of-the-art Ocean Research Vessel (Yard 3041), officially named ORV Sagar Manthan, was launched today at the Rishi Bankim Shipyard, Kolkata.

Designed, engineered, and constructed by defense public sector undertaking Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE) for the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), the vessel was officially launched through virtual presence by Dr. Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister of Earth Sciences, Government of India, with his spouse Mrs Manju Singh, who named the vessel, keeping with the tradition. The event was held in the august presence of Dr T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, who was joined by his spouse, Mrs Kavita Ellanti, for the ship launch in Kolkata.

Hon'ble Minister highlighted National Pride, Global Ocean Geopolitics, and Atmanirbharta. Delivering the keynote address (virtual), Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister of Earth Sciences, termed the occasion a "red letter day" for NCPOR, the Ministry, and the nation. He praised the team for achieving the launch within just two years of contract signing and barely five months after keel laying, hailing it as an exceptional display of efficiency.

Highlighting the strategic and scientific necessity of the vessel, Dr Jitendra Singh (through his message) conveyed: "This fine ship is India’s first advanced Ocean Research Vessel built by GRSE, displaying the required thrust towards Atmanirbharta and self-reliance that Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji has been laying so much stress on. Knowledge is strength, and this knowledge can only be gained through research. Today, the world knows very little about our oceans, yet they provide vital inputs about melting polar glaciers, maritime impact, and climate dynamics. Solid data collected by vessels like ORV Sagar Manthan will allow India to lead the global path in disaster prevention, take corrective environmental measures, and play a pivotal role in global ocean geopolitics."

Dr Singh noted that the feature-rich ORV Sagar Manthan will gradually replace the iconic 43-year-old ORV Sagar Kanya (procured from Germany in 1983), commending MoES plans to acquire more oceanographic vessels and a Polar Research Vessel in the near future.

MoES Secretary emphasised Scientific Capabilities and Indigenous Transition

In his address, Dr T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, expressed pride in India’s policy shift from acquiring research platforms abroad to building them domestically.

Elaborating the core scientific impact, Dr T. Srinivasa Kumar remarked:

"As an oceanographer, I have witnessed first-hand the immense value of ocean research. It is the foundation for understanding climate challenges, predicting tsunamis, and strengthening maritime capabilities. The capabilities of this new ORV excite me as a scientist. It will feature underway swath multibeam surveys, geophysical profiling, atmospheric observations, and water column sampling. GRSE has passed a complex challenge with flying colours, proving that India is among the select few nations capable of designing and constructing such complex platforms."

Project Background and Strategic Significance

Constructed under Vertical-4 (Deep Ocean Survey and Exploration) of the Government of India's flagship Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) at an approximate cost of Rs. 840 Crore, ORV Sagar Manthan is an all-weather, multidisciplinary platform. It is engineered to operate in extreme oceanic environments, including the Southern Ocean, with a projected service life of 30 years.

Key Technical & Operational Features

Advanced Equipment: Integrated with dynamic positioning, multibeam bathymetry, multichannel seismic systems, sub-bottom profiling, weather radar, drop keels, and deployment facilities for Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROV) and Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV).

Research Spectrum: Will support multidisciplinary exploration along the Indian Ocean mid-oceanic ridges to identify multi-metal hydrothermal sulphide mineralisation, establish environmental baselines, collect upper-air data, and undertake CTD profiling.

Dual-Class Certification: Built in full compliance with international regulatory standards under dual-class certification by the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS) and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS).

Project Milestones: Following contract signing in July 2024, first steel cutting on November 29, 2024, and Keel Laying on April 08, 2026, the vessel successfully transitioned from the erection dock to the construction dock today.

Following its launch, superstructure erection, system integration, and extensive sea trials will proceed before its final delivery for commissioning to NCPOR/MoES, which is scheduled for 2028.

The ceremony featured key ceremonial milestones conducted by distinguished dignitaries. After the welcome address by Cmdr PR Hari, C&MD, GRSE, the Launching & Naming Ceremony of Yard 3041 through the official Unveiling of the Name Plaque was done in the presence of Dr MV Ramanamurthy, Mission Director, Deep Ocean Mission and Dr Thamban Meloth, Director, NCPOR, MoES. Marking the flagship moment of the occasion, the formal Launching of the Ship was successfully executed by officially transferring the advanced vessel into the water to begin its next phase of construction.

Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

India to Debut in Eleven New Skills at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026

09 SEP 2026 12:55PM by PIB Delhi

India is set to expand its global skills footprint with first-time participation in eleven new skill categories at the 48th WorldSkills Competition, to be held in Shanghai, China, from 22 to 27 September 2026.

Team Skill India will participate in 63 out of 64 skills, with a contingent of nearly 70 competitors, making it one of India’s largest and most diverse representations at WorldSkills to date.

The eleven new skills in which India will compete for the first time are Dental Prosthetics, Digital Interactive Media Design, Intelligent Security Technology, Landscape Gardening, Optoelectronic Technology, Retail Sales, Unmanned Aerial Systems, Industrial Mechanics, Software Testing and Heavy Vehicle Technology, Aircraft Maintenance.

India’s participation in these new categories reflects the growing depth and maturity of the country’s skilling ecosystem, which is expanding from strong foundations in traditional trades to advanced technologies, specialised services, creative industries and next-generation industrial capabilities.

The participation is being led under the aegis of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) driving India’s WorldSkills preparation through close collaboration with industry partners, training institutions and domain experts.

Speaking on India’s participation, Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said, “India’s participation in these new skills reflects the evolution of our skilling ecosystem towards future-facing and globally relevant capabilities. headline: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya to Chair National Conference on Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) to be Held in Mumbai on 11–12 September 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Labour & Employment

Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya to Chair National Conference on Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) to be Held in Mumbai on 11–12 September 2026

Conference to Facilitate Sharing of Best Practices and Successful Interventions by States/UTs, Review Progress on Key Initiatives for Welfare of Construction Workers

09 SEP 2026 12:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Maharashtra, is organising a National Conference on Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) in Mumbai on 11–12 September 2026, under the chairmanship of Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister of Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports. The Conference will be attended by Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Labour Ministers and senior officials from States/UTs, Chairpersons and Secretaries of BOCW Welfare Boards and senior officers from Central and State governments.

The construction sector is among the largest sources of employment in the country and supports the livelihoods of millions of workers. With the implementation of the new Labour Codes, the Conference provides an important platform to take stock of the evolving BOCW framework and strengthen the functioning of Welfare Boards. Deliberations will cover statutory responsibilities, worker registration, welfare delivery, monitoring and utilisation of welfare funds, as well as opportunities for greater convergence and technology-enabled service delivery.

An important component of the Conference will be the sharing of innovative practices and successful interventions by the State BOCW Welfare Boards. The discussions are intended to facilitate cross-learning and identify approaches that can be adapted and replicated to improve the reach and effectiveness of welfare measures for construction workers.

The Conference will also review progress on three major initiatives launched at the National Labour Conference held in New Delhi in November 2025—the State BOCW Digital Labour Chowk, Labour Chowk-cum-Facilitation Centres and Online BOCW Cess Collection Portal. These initiatives seek to strengthen employment facilitation, provide more dignified and accessible worker-centric services, and improve transparency and efficiency in cess collection and monitoring.

The two-day programme will further deliberate on International Labour Mobility Pathways, skilling and employment opportunities, labour statistics and the labour stack. The Conference is aimed at building stronger coordination between the Centre, States/UTs and BOCW Welfare Boards, identifying implementation gaps and establishing priority actions for more effective and accessible delivery of social security, welfare and employment opportunities to construction workers.

headline: CAQM takes serious note of HSPCB’s non-compliance with its directions; Seeks explanation in review meeting
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

CAQM takes serious note of HSPCB’s non-compliance with its directions; Seeks explanation in review meeting

09 SEP 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

A review meeting was held on 08.09.2026 under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), with the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) regarding compliance with the Commission’s Statutory Directions, which mandate the registration of all C&D projects having a plot area of 500 sq. metres or above and the installation of functional video monitoring systems on the State/GNCTD web portal for remote monitoring of dust mitigation measures.

CAQM has been undertaking sample-based remote monitoring of C&D sites through the web portal of the HSPCB since 2024. During the monitoring exercises, several discrepancies have been observed, including incomplete/ insufficient web-camera links, incorrect User ID/ Password, links prompting installation of mobile applications, non-working web links and cameras remaining offline despite successful login. These discrepancies have been communicated to HSPCB from time to time for necessary corrective action(s).

During the remote monitoring exercise conducted by CAQM through the HSPCB portal from 19.06.2026 to 22.06.2026, it was observed that out of 213 active C&D sites registered in Panipat, 457 in Sonipat, 168 in Faridabad, 691 in Gurugram (North) and 484 in Gurugram (South), web-camera links at most of the sites were found to be non-functional. Functional links were available only at 4 sites in Faridabad, 6 sites in Gurugram (North) and 5 sites in Gurugram (South). The observations were communicated to HSPCB on 08.07.2026.

CAQM has also earlier advised HSPCB to deploy a dedicated team for effective remote monitoring through the portal. However, neither such team was deployed nor any substantial improvement was observed. The non-functioning of web-camera links has consequently defeated the very purpose of the web portal for effective remote monitoring of C&D sites and verification of dust-control measures.

Taking serious note of the continued discrepancies and non-compliance by HSPCB, the Commission has treated the matter as willful non-compliance on the part of the designated authority responsible for enforcement of the Commission’s Directions. CAQM called upon HSPCB for the review meeting, to furnish the requisite information, detailed response and report with respect to the notices issued to it, indicating the complete status of compliance. In response, HSPCB apprised the Commission of the compliance status and the steps undertaken towards implementation of CAQM’s Statutory Directions.

Further, in the review meeting, HSPCB has been directed to ensure strict compliance with all Order(s)/ Statutory Direction(s) issued by the Commission and to take necessary corrective measures including closure of non-compliant sites, for ensuring effective and uninterrupted remote monitoring of C&D sites. The concerned authorities were also directed to strengthen monitoring and enforcement mechanisms so that the prescribed dust mitigation measures are effectively implemented at C&D sites.

The Commission reiterated that effective implementation of its Statutory Directions by concerned agencies is critical for prevention and abatement of air pollution in NCR. CAQM emphasised that concerned agencies must ensure timely compliance with the Order(s)/ Statutory Direction(s) issued by CAQM in letter and spirit and strengthen monitoring & enforcement mechanism for effective on-ground implementation. The Commission will continue to closely monitor compliance and take necessary measures towards effective mitigation of air pollution in the region.

NITI Aayog’s National Workshop on Strengthening Ayush Ecosystem brings together Centre, over 30 States and UTs

09 SEP 2026 12:25PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, called upon States and Union Territories to strengthen the delivery of accessible, people-centric and quality Ayush services across the country. Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas highlighted the importance of technology-integrated and evidence-based approaches to integrative healthcare, with the potential to improve health outcomes in India and beyond.

Every School, A Model School

PM SHRI and India's Push for Future-Ready Schools

09 SEP 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi

Launched on 7 September 2022, the Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) Scheme seeks to develop over 14,500 exemplar schools aligned with the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. With a total outlay of ₹27,360 crore across 2022–23 to 2026–27, the scheme strengthens infrastructure, pedagogy, inclusion, and sustainability, while equipping students with 21st-century skills. As of July 2026, 13,092 schools - around 90% of the target- have been selected across 36 States/UTs including schools under KVS, NVS, and NCERT. The schools are selected through a three-stage Challenge Mode based on defined quality benchmarks. Envisioned as mentor institutions for neighbouring schools, PM SHRI schools mark a shift from infrastructure-centric development towards holistic, equitable, and future-ready education.

PM SHRI: Building Schools That Lead by Example

India is witnessing a significant transformation in its school education system, marked by a growing emphasis on quality, equity, inclusion, and future-ready learning. With 14.71 lakh schools serving more than 24.69 crore students, the education system is increasingly focused on enhancing learning outcomes and creating enabling environments that support the holistic development of every learner. The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 furnishes the overarching framework for this transformation, while the PM SHRI initiative operationalizes its vision at the school level, translating policy intent into institutional practice. Launched on 7 September 2022, the Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) Scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education. The scheme seeks to qualitatively strengthen existing schools and develop them as exemplar institutions demonstrating the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. With a total project cost of ₹27,360 crore, the scheme focuses on strengthening more than 14,500 existing schools as exemplar institutions. These schools are envisioned to provide safe, stimulating, and welcoming learning environments, supported by quality infrastructure, appropriate learning resources, and diverse learning experiences.

As of July 2026, 13,092 schools have been selected as PM SHRI Schools across States and Union Territories, including schools under the Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) and National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT). This represents around 90% of the envisaged target. The scheme is expected to benefit more than 20 lakh students directly.

Strategic Focus of PM SHRI

The scheme extends support beyond strengthening individual schools. PM SHRI schools are envisioned as models for their regions, sharing their practices and supporting neighbouring schools through mentoring, handholding, collaboration and clustering. This is intended to create a ripple effect, enabling more schools to develop towards exemplar standards over time.

At the core of the scheme is a vision of education that fosters lifelong learning and equips students with the capacity and disposition to learn, unlearn and relearn. The broader objective is to develop engaged, productive and responsible citizens capable of contributing to the creation of an equitable, inclusive and plural society.

Strengthening School Education Through PM SHRI

The Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) scheme is being implemented over five years, from 2022–23 to 2026–27. The scheme has a total project cost of ₹27,360 crore, including a Central share of ₹18,128 crore. The central share of approved Project Approval Board (PAB) outlay rose from ₹2,520 crore in 2023–24 to ₹5,224 crore in 2026–27. This marks an increase of around 107%, reflecting the growing scale of investment in strengthening PM SHRI schools.

PM SHRI Schools: Advancing the Vision of NEP 2020

PM SHRI Scheme aims to showcase all the components of the National Education Policy 2020 and focuses not only on cognitive development but also on creating holistic and well-rounded individuals equipped with key 21st century skills. The scheme focuses on creating an equitable, inclusive, and joyful learning environment that caters to diverse backgrounds and varied academic abilities. These schools are designed to engage students actively in their learning process, ensuring that every child feels welcomed, cared for, and supported in a safe and stimulating environment.

Key Dimensions of Quality and Excellence under PM SHRI

PM SHRI Schools are designed as exemplar schools that demonstrate the key principles of NEP 2020 through quality education, modern infrastructure, inclusive practices and sustainable development.

Inclusive Learning: Provides high-quality, equitable, and joyful education while addressing diverse backgrounds, multilingual needs, and different learning abilities.

Mentorship: PM SHRI Schools will serve as exemplar schools and provide leadership and mentorship to other schools in their regions.

Green Schools: Promote sustainable and environment-friendly practices as an important school quality benchmark.

Experiential Learning: Emphasizes experiential, holistic, integrated, inquiry-based, and learner-centered approaches, including play and toy-based learning in the foundational years.

Learning Outcomes: Focuses on curriculum, pedagogy and assessment to strengthen learning outcomes and the application of knowledge.

Quality Infrastructure: Involves assessing school infrastructure on parameters including adequacy, functionality, aesthetics and safety.

Future Ready Skills: Promotes exposure to 21st century skills and links schools with the local entrepreneurial ecosystem.

Quality Assessment: The School Quality Assessment Framework (SQAF) provides a structured mechanism to assess and monitor the quality of PM SHRI Schools.

The six pillars of PM SHRI schools

The PM SHRI schools scheme is based on the development of sub-domains of six major pillars derived from 9 chapters of NEP 2020, which are as follows:

How PM SHRI Schools Transform School Education

Learning Designed Around the Child

PM SHRI schools follow either the CBSE or the relevant State or Union Territory syllabus according to their affiliation. Their curriculum follows the National Curriculum Framework or State Curriculum Framework developed in accordance with the 5+3+3+4 curricular and pedagogical structure under NEP 2020. States and Union Territories have flexibility to contextualise the curriculum according to local needs while adhering to core principles and constitutional values.

PM SHRI Schools also promote experiential learning through bagless days,

internships with local artisans, study of local arts, crafts and traditions, celebration of important cultural events, and preservation of indigenous knowledge and practices.

Equity, Inclusion and Multilingual Learning

PMSHRI schools have played a pivotal role in providing inclusive and equitable education, ensuring that students from diverse backgrounds, including rural and underserved communities, have access to high-quality education. By focusing on bridging educational disparities, these schools have helped create a more equitable learning environment across India.

The scheme also promotes the use of the mother tongue, local or regional language as the medium of teaching and learning, particularly in the early grades. The latest UDISE+ 2025–26 data records 6,102 Sanskrit teachers, 1,994 Urdu teachers, and 9,152 regional language teachers in PM SHRI schools.

It also encourages community participation in supporting learning through local languages. This approach is crucial for ensuring that every child develops strong foundational literacy and numeracy skills.

Technology Enabled Learning

A significant achievement of PM SHRI Schools lies in the systematic integration of technology into the teaching–learning environment. The provision of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) facilities, smart classrooms, internet connectivity, digital learning platforms, and STEM-based programmes is contributing to the creation of more interactive, experiential, and learner-centred educational environments. These interventions not only enhance access to diverse learning resources but also support the development of digital literacy, technological competencies, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Platforms such as DIKSHA serve as repositories of high-quality digital educational resources and facilitate the sharing and dissemination of learning materials among teachers and students, thereby strengthening technology-enabled pedagogical practices.

Holistic Student Development

PM SHRI Schools adopt a holistic approach to student development by integrating academic learning with extracurricular activities, sports, arts, and life-skills education. This multidimensional approach extends beyond conventional academic achievement to foster the development of leadership capabilities, creativity, socio-emotional competencies, and interpersonal skills. By providing opportunities for diverse forms of learning and participation, the schools seek to equip students with the competencies, resilience, and adaptability required to navigate future educational, professional, and social challenges.

Empowering Teachers and School Leaders

PM SHRI Schools seek to strengthen teacher capacity and institutional leadership through structured professional development initiatives supported by District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs). Under the initiative, financial assistance of up to ₹3 lakh per DIET is provided for capacity-building programmes, while support of up to ₹2,500 per teacher is extended for the training of subject teachers, principals, special educators, ICT teachers, and master trainers.

Principals are provided training in educational leadership, school management, and competency-based pedagogical planning, enabling them to strengthen institutional planning and academic governance. Teachers receive professional development in areas including the Holistic Progress Card, school safety, mental health and well-being, first-level counselling, and ICT integration. These interventions seek to enhance pedagogical competencies, strengthen school leadership, and promote continuous professional development among educational personnel.

A Growing National Network

The PM SHRI initiative has established a substantial national network comprising 13,092 selected schools across States and Union Territories, including institutions under the Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), and National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT). The initiative has achieved extensive geographical coverage, encompassing 725 districts and 8,340 blocks/ULBs, thereby establishing a broad institutional and spatial footprint across the country.

Among the 13,092 selected schools, 1,305 are primary schools, 3,102 upper primary schools, 3,141 secondary schools, and 5,544 higher secondary schools. The network further includes 80 Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs), 913 KVS schools, 620 NVS schools, and 4 NCERT schools. The scale and diversity of this network demonstrate the expanding reach of PM SHRI Schools.

Selection Built on Quality Benchmarks

Selection of PM SHRI schools is done through Challenge Mode, wherein Schools compete for support to become exemplar schools. Selection is done through a three-stage process with definite timelines, which is as follows:

Stage 1: Signing of Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)

States and Union Territories (UTs) enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Centre, outlining their commitments towards providing the requisite support and enabling the selected schools to achieve the prescribed quality standards for PM SHRI Schools.

Stage 2: Identification of Eligible Schools

A pool of schools eligible for selection as PM SHRI Schools is identified on the basis of prescribed minimum benchmarks and relevant indicators available through the UDISE+ data.

Stage 3: Selection through the Challenge Method

Eligible schools identified in Stage 2 participate in a challenge-based selection process to demonstrate compliance with specified criteria. Schools compete against the prescribed challenge conditions, with fulfilment of the stipulated requirements.

Fulfillment of conditions is verified and certified through physical inspection by the respective States/UTs, KVS, or NVS authorities, and recommend the list of schools to the Ministry.

An Expert Committee headed by the Secretary (SE&L), at the Ministry of Education, is constituted for final selection of schools. Schools must meet minimum standards such as a pucca building, barrier-free access, safety measures, separate toilets, drinking water, hand-washing facilities, electricity, ID cards for teachers, enrolment at Elementary and Senior Secondary levels must be more than the State average enrolment and library or sports facilities. For the Challenge Method, schools in urban areas are required to secure a minimum score of 70 percent, while schools in rural areas require a minimum of 60 percent. The assessment covers infrastructure, learning outcomes, pedagogy, PM POSHAN, vocational education, green initiatives, and stakeholder commitment.

Schools as Models for Wider Change

PM SHRI represents a paradigm shift from an infrastructure-centric approach to school development towards the establishment of holistic, inclusive, equitable, and future-ready learning institutions. The initiative operationalises the vision and priorities of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 by emphasising quality and competency-based learning, continuous teacher professional development, technology-enabled education, and the creation of a safe, inclusive, and enabling school environment.

As exemplar institutions, PM SHRI Schools are envisaged to demonstrate and disseminate innovative educational practices that can be adapted and replicated by neighbouring schools, thereby contributing to broader systemic improvements in school education. The overarching objective is to foster capable, confident, creative, and responsible learners, equipped with the knowledge, skills, and values required to participate meaningfully in a more equitable, inclusive, and future-ready India.

headline: TDB-DST Supports M/s Ceramat Private Limited for Commercialisation of 3D-Printed Patient-Specific Bone Grafts
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

TDB-DST Supports M/s Ceramat Private Limited for Commercialisation of 3D-Printed Patient-Specific Bone Grafts

09 SEP 2026 11:53AM by PIB Delhi

Advancing India’s capabilities in high-end medical technology and strengthening indigenous alternatives to imported healthcare products, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has extended financial assistance to M/s Ceramat Private Limited, Palghar, Maharashtra, for the project titled “Calcium Phosphate based Standard and Customized Patient Specific Grafts by 3D Printing via Digital Light Processing Technique and Extrusion-based Equipment.” The project aims to commercialise advanced, patient-specific bone grafts using indigenously manufactured bioceramic materials and 3D printing technologies.

Ceramat Private Limited has been established with a focus on developing and commercialising indigenous technologies in bio-ceramics and advanced ceramics, with the objective of creating high-quality import substitutes for critical applications. The company’s product portfolio includes technologically intensive biomaterials such as hydroxyapatite, beta-tricalcium phosphate, biphasic calcium phosphate and bioactive glass, serving applications across orthopaedics, oral care, cosmetics and industrial sectors.

Hydroxyapatite and beta-tricalcium phosphate are calcium phosphate-based biomaterials that closely resemble the mineral composition of natural bone and are widely used in bone grafts and implant applications. A significant proportion of such advanced bone graft products available in India are currently imported. While Ceramat already manufactures bone grafts and granules through conventional processes, producing customised grafts matching the anatomy of individual patients presents a more complex manufacturing challenge.

The proposed project seeks to address this gap by integrating 3D printing with indigenously manufactured bioceramic raw materials. The company plans to develop standard as well as customised patient-specific grafts through two complementary approaches—Digital Light Processing (DLP)-based 3D printing and extrusion-based 3D printing. These technologies will enable greater flexibility in developing complex geometries and customised structures suited to specific clinical requirements.

The use of indigenous calcium phosphate-based materials in combination with advanced additive manufacturing is expected to expand Ceramet’s existing biomaterials capabilities from conventional graft products to more sophisticated, digitally designed and patient-specific solutions. The initiative will also enable the company to offer a broader range of bioceramic and orthobiological products through an integrated domestic manufacturing ecosystem.

The project is aligned with the Government of India’s emphasis on Aatmanirbhar Bharat, advanced manufacturing and indigenous medical technology development. By developing patient-specific graft manufacturing capabilities within the country, the initiative is expected to reduce dependence on imported bioceramic and orthobiological products, strengthen domestic supply chains and create a platform with potential for global markets.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “India’s transition from being a technology consumer to a technology developer requires indigenous capabilities in specialised and high-value areas of healthcare. The development of advanced bio-ceramics combined with 3D printing can open new possibilities for personalised medical solutions while reducing dependence on imported products. TDB is committed to supporting technologies that bring Indian innovation from development to commercial application and strengthen our capabilities in globally competitive medical manufacturing.”

headline: Financial Intelligence Unit- India (FIU-IND) issues notices for non-compliance to 15 Virtual Digital Assets Service providers (VDA SPs) under Section 13 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PML) Act, 2002
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

Financial Intelligence Unit- India (FIU-IND) issues notices for non-compliance to 15 Virtual Digital Assets Service providers (VDA SPs) under Section 13 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PML) Act, 2002

09 SEP 2026 11:12AM by PIB Delhi

As part of compliance action against non-compliant entities, the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) has issued notices for non-compliance to following fifteen (15) Virtual Digital Assets Service Providers (VDA SPs) under Section 13 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002(PMLA) as under:-

S. No | Trade Name | Entity Name

1 | Weex | Weex International Exchange LTD

2 | Blofin | BLF Global Limited

3 | Rezorex | RezorEx

4 | Bitunix | Bitunix LLC

5 | DigiFinex | DigiFinex Ltd

6 | Toobit | Hopeful Technology Co. Ltd.

7 | XT.com | Fibtc Ltd/ XT TECHNICAL PTE. LTD.

8 | Latoken | LAtrade Ltd

9 | WOO X | Wootech Limited

10 | Pionex | Marketa Trading Inc.

11 | ChangeNow | CHN Group LLC

12 | SimpleSwap | SimpleSwap LTD

13 | Fixedfloat | FFGX Group LLC

14 | WhiteBIT | UAB Clear White Technologies

15 | Guardarian | FinSeven CZ

Further, the Director, FIU-IND, being the nodal officer in pursuance of Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 read with rule 3(1)(d) of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2025, has also issued notices with respect to the aforesaid entities to takedown the application/URLs for public access which have been found to be operating illegally without complying with the relevant provisions of the PMLA in India.

Virtual Digital Assets Service Providers (VDA SPs) were brought into the ambit of Anti Money Laundering/Counter Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) framework under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 in March 2023.

The VDA SPs operating in India (whether offshore or onshore) and engaged in activities like exchange between virtual digital assets and fiat currencies, transfer of virtual digital assets, safekeeping or administration of virtual digital assets or instruments enabling control over virtual digital assets etc. are required to be registered with FIU-IND as Reporting Entity and comply with the set of obligations as mandated under Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002(PMLA) and Rules framed there under. These obligations are activity-based and are not contingent on physical presence of the entity in India. The regulation casts reporting, record keeping, and other obligations on the VDA SPs under the PML Act which also includes registration with the FIU-IND.

It is pertinent to mention for the safety and awareness of general public that the Crypto products and NFTs are unregulated and can be highly risky. There may be no regulatory recourse for any loss from such transactions.
